TextBlock.Text: THEATRE Timor Sea
DATE 26 October 2028 · 1610 local
SIDE Royal Australian Navy
WINDOW 60 min, closes at 90
Canberra class LHD. Photo: Nick-D · CC BY-SA 4.0 · cropped
"Air superiority is not guaranteed. It must be earned every day."
- Gen. Kenneth S. Wilsbach, Chief of Staff, US Air Force, 2025

TIMOR SEA, late afternoon. Rig Seventeen has not answered its shore office since the weekend. Thirty contract staff are still aboard, and the armed Meridian contractors holding the platform have a helicopter deck, a shore battery on the Timor coast to the north and an air-defence vehicle they were not supposed to have.

Indonesia has asked for help and set the boundary: you may cover an evacuation, you may not level the installation. CHOULES is in company with CANBERRA, and the US Marine Rotational Force in Darwin has lent the lift for one afternoon at the end of its rotation: a Super Stallion and an Osprey, airborne south of the rig. Canberra has two Army Apaches on deck, armed with Hellfire and ready to launch, for the patrol boats, and two Romeos. Meridian has two missile boats closing from the north and north-west, a fast gunboat coming in from the east, and a Hind gunship expected to join after fifteen minutes. Those are military targets; the civilian platform and passing traffic are not.

Bring BOTH lifters over the platform, within three miles of it, and hold them there for three minutes while the crew is loaded - half go in each aircraft. AMPHIBIOUS CONTROL will tell you when everybody is aboard. Then bring both lifters back to the amphibious group before the light goes. Lose either lifter and the people in it are lost with her. Not every platform out here is hostile, and most of this coast is working its ordinary week.
COMMAND NET: A mission-specific tactical report follows eight minutes after the start. It is advice from the command team, not a new sensor detection.

FORWARD RECON: MOTH 11, a small RQ-7 reconnaissance UAV, joins over the local approach at minute ten, allowing time for initial air-defence suppression. Two reserve UAVs are at the forward recovery section from the start. They are unarmed, have finite fuel and a local recovery field. Use their sensors to classify the military installations and update strike aimpoints. The small airframes are vulnerable; no scripted reveal grants a target solution. Keep a recovery margin and reposition the initial track as needed.
Commodore Alex Mercer; Captain Ratna Prasetyo, Indonesian Navy (TNI-AL), embarked
COMMANDER'S INTENT

The platform is not a target. The armed contractors on its upper deck are Captain Prasetyo's problem afterwards and not yours now. Two lift aircraft, and it takes both to bring thirty people and their injured off a helideck. Three armed patrol craft are closing from different directions, with a gunship expected later. Keep them off the lifters until everybody is back aboard.
• Hold both lifters at the rig until the crew is aboard, then bring both back to the amphibious group
• Leave the civilian platform standing
• Keep both amphibious ships afloat
• Obtain a current classification of the land target area

HMAS Choules and HMAS Canberra with two Army AH-64E Apaches and two MH-60R, a USMC CH-53E and MV-22B on loan from the Darwin rotational force for the lift, and your escort. Ashore: a launcher site, a VL MICA battery, a Sosna vehicle and a technical. At sea: two missile boats and a fast gunboat closing on the rig. A Hind gunship joins after fifteen minutes. Forward RQ-7 section: two reserve UAVs at a local strip; Moth 11 joins at minute ten.

The planned window is 60 minutes. At that minute Command signals that you are behind schedule and holds the line for about 30 minutes more; the operation is closed at 90 minutes and the main task will be recorded as failed.
RULES OF ENGAGEMENT
All designated neutral contacts are protected. A protected neutral loss cancels the operation. Identify before you shoot.
